title: Rose Rayhaan by Rotana
visualBrief: Dubai’s slender four-lobed blue-glass hotel with silver vertical recesses, physical gold eye rings and cornices, four curved silver crown petals, crossing tip ribbons, a sphere and offset northeast spire.

nativeAxes.origin: Mapped rectangular envelope at reconstructed street datum

reconstruction.massing: The exact-QID footprint supplies the narrow rectangular site envelope. Four intersecting convex glass lobes reconstruct the paired curved bays visible in the operator’s completed-building aerial photograph; the map rectangle is not extruded as the tower facade.
reconstruction.facade: Operator daytime photographs and the facade-access contractor establish blue/silver mirrored glass, narrow gold rings and gold cornices. Repeated glass panes, thin physical frames, inset strips and elliptical gold ornament remain geometry at metric scale.
reconstruction.crown: The current operator aerial establishes four silver tapering petals bordered by pale ribs, neighboring black/white horizontal bands, interlaced tip ribbons, a sphere and offset mast. Intermediate crown heights and curve profiles are photo reconstructions within the verified333m final envelope.
reconstruction.entry: The southwest road-facing entry has a small canopy and glazed door bays. Fine canopy/door dimensions are approximate; adjacent neighboring towers and rear parking remain separate map context.

geographicProposal.orientationConfidence: exact identity plus operator aerial direction and reconstructed northeast mast
geographicProposal.notes: Fresh OSM API on 2026-10-10 confirms exact Q648338 whole 64890199 and sub-millimeter agreement with the stored prior georeferencing outline. Operator aerial 0 looks southeast along the road toward the independently identified Burj Khalifa, fixing the northeast offset mast behind its petal. Mast [5.7,0], doorway/canopy and lobed radii remain photo reconstructions, not separately surveyed mapped features. scaleBasis: Published owner/architect/contractor heights and distinguishing construction systems; map footprint for local orientation, with reconstructed details declared separately.
geometrySource: Original deterministic exterior geometry; no downloaded meshes or copied photographic textures. Footprint-derived registration includes separately attributed OpenStreetMap evidence.
sourceLicense: Original reconstruction under repository license. Map-derived plan evidence: © OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL-1.0. Reference publications are linked, not redistributed.
materialMethod: Canonical shared material graphs bound through molenSurface extras with metric coordinates divided by central repeat meters. Vertex colors provide component tint. Glass retains opaque metallic-roughness PBR; no bitmap texture copies per model.
reviewStatus: source-geometry; near/far and shared-material captures pending
limitations: Original 623480-triangle, 52717200-byte master remains exactly reproducible from unchanged recipe. Reviewed source/four browser levels retain four intersecting convex blue-glass lobes, silver vertical recesses, gold eyes/cornices, four curved silver crown petals and pale boundary ribs, alternating dark/light neighboring bands, crossing tip ribbons, sphere, offset northeast mast and southwest entry canopy. The original 245–246 m gap is closed with a shoulder panel. Whole facade backing panels and continuous strips replace per-pane beams; thin eye rings use planar ribbons rather than tubular segments. Skyline averages trim colour and omits small eyes/collars/door frames, district/street aggregate eyes and panel cadence and omit/aggregate fine crown seams; skyline/district use shallow curved petal boundary strips while street/close-up retain solid ribs; close-up retains all 248 eye rings at reduced arc sampling, 128 angular samples and closed boundary ribs. Two canonical shared graphs approximate stone and silver/gold coated metal; three draw groups and zero embedded images. Lobed radii, intermediate crown heights, leaf phase, entry/canopy and 5.7 m mast offset are photo reconstructions; only rectangular site envelope is mapped. Operator 72 / CVU 71 storeys remain distinct; their shared 333 m architectural height sets tip. Moving access equipment, signage, interiors and animated lighting excluded. Finite along-ray 1.5/.75/.3/.1 m allowances exclude omitted narrow eyes, mullions and collars; no global surface-distance, surveyed grade or physical-device claim.
importReason: Preserve thin facade frames, panel joints and crown/antenna details until a measured LOD chain is authored.
